entries.nodal_ministry: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
entries.text: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme PMEGP Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Credit-linked subsidy programme to generate self-employment opportunities through establishment of micro-enterprises in manufacturing and service sectors. Any individual above 18 years of age. At least VIII standard pass for projects costing above Rs.10 lakh in manufacturing and above Rs.5 lakh in service sector. Only new projects are eligible; existing units or units that have availed government subsidy under other schemes are not eligible. Self Help Groups (SHGs), Institutions registered under Societies Registration Act 1860, Production Co-operative Societies, and Charitable Trusts are also eligible. 15% to 35% margin money subsidy. Max project cost: ₹50 Lakh for manufacturing, ₹20 Lakh for services. Beneficiary contribution is 5% to 10%. employment manufacturing services margin-money subsidy kvic micro-enterprise ALL Online via KVIC PMEGP Portal / Jan Samarth Step 1: Visit the official PMEGP e-Portal (kviconline.gov.in) or Jan Samarth platform. Step 2: Click 'Apply Online' for New Enterprise or 2nd Loan for Upgradation. Step 3: Enter Aadhaar number, PAN, applicant personal details, and social category. Step 4: Select Sponsoring Agency (KVIC, KVIB, or District Industries Centre - DIC). Step 5: Select Financing Bank Branch where loan is sought. Step 6: Upload Detailed Project Report (DPR), educational certificate (Class 8th pass), caste certificate, and rural area certificate. Step 7: Submit application to generate Unique Application ID and download acknowledgement slip. Step 8: Undergo DIC/KVIC task force scrutiny followed by electronic forwarding to the selected bank branch. Step 9: Bank conducts sanction and physical unit verification; complete mandatory EDP training to receive margin money subsidy in escrow.
entries.snippet: Credit-linked subsidy programme to generate self-employment opportunities through establishment of micro-enterprises in manufacturing and service sectors.

entries.scheme_name: Credit Guarantee Scheme for Micro & Small Enterprises
entries.nodal_ministry: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
entries.text: Credit Guarantee Scheme for Micro & Small Enterprises CGTMSE Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Facilitates collateral-free credit facilities (term loans and working capital) up to ₹5 Crore from commercial banks and financial institutions for micro and small enterprises. Both new and existing Micro and Small Enterprises (MSEs) engaged in manufacturing or service activities. Retail trade and wholesale trade are also covered up to eligible limits. Borrower unit must hold valid Udyam Registration and GST Registration. Facility covers loans up to ₹500 Lakh without third-party guarantee or collateral security. Collateral-free credit up to ₹5 Crore with guarantee coverage of 75% to 85% (up to 85% for women entrepreneurs, SC/ST, and units in NER/Aspirational districts). collateral-free bank-loan guarantee sidbi working-capital term-loan ALL Through Member Lending Institutions (MLIs) / Jan Samarth Step 1: Formulate comprehensive business plan and project report with fund requirement up to ₹5 Crore. Step 2: Approach any CGTMSE Member Lending Institution (Scheduled Commercial Bank, SIDBI, RRB, or NBFC). Step 3: Apply for collateral-free MSME credit facility (term loan and/or working capital). Step 4: Bank conducts appraisal and issues in-principle sanction without requiring collateral or third-party guarantee. Step 5: Lending bank submits borrower profile directly to CGTMSE digital portal for guarantee coverage. Step 6: CGTMSE issues digital guarantee cover (up to 85% for women/Micro units, 75% for others) upon payment of upfront guarantee fee. Step 7: Loan disbursement into borrower's operative account.
entries.snippet: Facilitates collateral-free credit facilities (term loans and working capital) up to ₹5 Crore from commercial banks and financial institutions for micro and small enterprises.

entries.nodal_ministry: Ministry of Finance - Department of Financial Services
entries.text: Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana - Shishu PMMY-Shishu Ministry of Finance - Department of Financial Services Micro-finance credit facility providing loans up to ₹50,000 for early-stage or very small micro-enterprises with minimal paperwork and zero collateral. Any Indian citizen who has a business plan for non-farm income-generating activity such as manufacturing, processing, trading, or service sector. Loan requirement is up to ₹50,000. No collateral required. Applicant must not be a defaulter to any bank or financial institution. Loans up to ₹50,000 at competitive bank interest rates, nil processing fee, and zero collateral security. mudra shishu micro-loan collateral-free small-shopkeeper vendor ALL Online via Jan Samarth / Bank Branch Step 1: Visit Jan Samarth portal (jansamarth.in) or visit nearest bank / MFI branch. Step 2: Complete basic registration with mobile number, Aadhaar, and business profile. Step 3: Select 'Business Activity Loan' -> 'MUDRA Shishu' category (up to ₹50,000). Step 4: Enter quotation of machinery/inventory to be purchased and supplier details. Step 5: Upload identity proof (Aadhaar/Voter ID), address proof, and applicant photograph. Step 6: Jan Samarth issues instant digital in-principle approval and routes application to chosen bank. Step 7: Bank verifies documents, executes loan agreement (zero processing fee, zero collateral), and disburses loan with MUDRA debit card.
entries.snippet: Micro-finance credit facility providing loans up to ₹50,000 for early-stage or very small micro-enterprises with minimal paperwork and zero collateral.

entries.nodal_ministry: Ministry of Finance - Department of Financial Services
entries.text: Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana - Kishore PMMY-Kishore Ministry of Finance - Department of Financial Services Mid-tier micro credit providing business loans from ₹50,000 to ₹5,00,000 for expanding micro business enterprises. Micro-enterprises that have already commenced operations and need funds between ₹50,000 and ₹5,00,000 for business expansion or machinery acquisition. Clean credit history and non-defaulter status. Valid business registration or establishment proof (GST / Shop & Est / Udyam). Term loan or working capital overdraft from ₹50,000 to ₹5,00,000 without collateral. mudra kishore expansion working-capital equipment-finance ALL Online via Jan Samarth / Bank Portals Step 1: Access Jan Samarth portal or partner bank MSME loan portal. Step 2: Register and select 'MUDRA Kishore' category (loan amount ₹50,000 to ₹5 Lakh). Step 3: Submit KYC documents (Aadhaar, PAN), business address proof, and Udyam Registration. Step 4: Provide last 6 to 12 months bank statements, sales turnover details, and machinery/equipment quotation. Step 5: Select preferred lending bank branch and submit digital application. Step 6: Receive digital in-principle sanction letter. Step 7: Bank conducts credit appraisal, opens loan account, and disburses credit without collateral.
entries.snippet: Mid-tier micro credit providing business loans from ₹50,000 to ₹5,00,000 for expanding micro business enterprises.

entries.scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana - Tarun & Tarun Plus
entries.nodal_ministry: Ministry of Finance - Department of Financial Services
entries.text: Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana - Tarun & Tarun Plus PMMY-Tarun Ministry of Finance - Department of Financial Services Flagship credit facility offering loans from ₹5 Lakh up to ₹20 Lakh (Tarun Plus) for scaling mature micro businesses. Established micro and small business units requiring higher capital for scaling. Loan requirement between ₹5,00,000 and ₹10,00,000 (and up to ₹20 Lakh under Tarun Plus for previous borrowers who successfully repaid Tarun loans). Documented operating history of at least 1-2 years with positive cash flows. Credit facility from ₹5 Lakh up to ₹20 Lakh without collateral requirement. mudra tarun growth-capital tarun-plus scaleup ALL Online via Jan Samarth / Bank Digital Lending Portals Step 1: Register on Jan Samarth portal or partner bank MSME lending website. Step 2: Select 'MUDRA Tarun' (₹5 Lakh to ₹10 Lakh) or 'Tarun Plus' (up to ₹20 Lakh for successful past borrowers). Step 3: Provide Udyam Registration Certificate, GSTIN, and past 1-2 years audited financial statements / ITR. Step 4: Upload Detailed Project Report (DPR) detailing expansion, machinery requirements, and projected cash flows. Step 5: Select lending institution and generate digital in-principle sanction. Step 6: Bank branch conducts loan evaluation and technical-economic feasibility check. Step 7: Sanction and disbursement of term loan and working capital limit under collateral-free guarantee.
entries.snippet: Flagship credit facility offering loans from ₹5 Lakh up to ₹20 Lakh (Tarun Plus) for scaling mature micro businesses.

entries.nodal_ministry: Ministry of Finance - Department of Financial Services
entries.text: Stand-Up India Scheme StandUp-India Ministry of Finance - Department of Financial Services Bank loans between ₹10 Lakh and ₹1 Crore to at least one Scheduled Caste (SC) or Scheduled Tribe (ST) borrower and at least one woman borrower per bank branch for setting up greenfield enterprises. SC/ST and/or woman entrepreneurs above 18 years of age. Loans under the scheme are available only for greenfield projects (the first-time venture of the beneficiary in manufacturing, services, agri-allied activities, or trading). In case of non-individual enterprises, 51% of the shareholding and controlling stake must be held by either SC/ST and/or women entrepreneur. Borrower should not be in default to any bank or financial institution. Composite loan (term loan and working capital) between ₹10 Lakh and ₹1 Crore covering up to 85% of total project cost. women-entrepreneurs sc-st greenfield bank-loan sidbi ALL Online via Stand-Up Mitra Portal / Jan Samarth Step 1: Visit the official Stand-Up Mitra portal (standupmitra.in). Step 2: Click 'Register' as a borrower and complete the eligibility profile check (SC, ST, or Woman entrepreneur with >= 51% shareholding). Step 3: Choose whether applying as 'Ready Borrower' (project report ready) or 'Trainee Borrower' (needing handholding support). Step 4: Fill in enterprise details: greenfield project in manufacturing, services, or trading sector (cost ₹10 Lakh to ₹1 Crore). Step 5: Upload KYC, Caste Certificate (for SC/ST), Udyam Registration, project report, and promoter margin proof (minimum 10-15%). Step 6: Select preferred bank branch from network of over 1.4 lakh bank branches nationwide. Step 7: Bank reviews application, sanctions composite loan (term loan + working capital), and provides credit guarantee coverage under NCGTC.
entries.snippet: Bank loans between ₹10 Lakh and ₹1 Crore to at least one Scheduled Caste (SC) or Scheduled Tribe (ST) borrower and at least one woman borrower per bank branch for setting up greenfield enterprises.

entries.nodal_ministry: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
entries.text: PM Vishwakarma Scheme PM-Vishwakarma Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises End-to-end holistic support for traditional artisans and craftspeople across 18 designated trades, including skill training, ₹15,000 toolkit incentive, and collateral-free credit at 5% interest. An artisan or craftsperson working with hands and tools, engaged in one of 18 family-based traditional trades. Minimum age of 18 years on the date of registration. The beneficiary should not have availed loans under similar credit-based schemes of Central or State Government (e.g. PMEGP, PM SVANidhi, Mudra) in the past 5 years. Registration is restricted to one member of the family. PM Vishwakarma Certificate & ID card, ₹15,000 toolkit incentive e-voucher, basic & advanced training with ₹500/day stipend, and collateral-free credit support up to ₹3 Lakh (₹1 Lakh tranche-1 and ₹2 Lakh tranche-2) at concessional interest rate of 5%. artisans traditional-trades toolkit subvention carpenter blacksmith crafts Artisans & Crafts Manufacturing Handicrafts Online via Common Services Centre (CSC) / PM Vishwakarma Portal Step 1: Artisan or craftsperson visits nearest Common Services Centre (CSC) with Aadhaar and Aadhaar-linked mobile number. Step 2: Complete biometric authentication and registration on the PM Vishwakarma Portal (pmvishwakarma.gov.in). Step 3: Select recognized traditional trade (e.g. carpenter, blacksmith, potter, tailor, cobbler, mason, etc.). Step 4: Level 1 verification: Scrutiny by Gram Panchayat / Urban Local Body (ULB) chairman. Step 5: Level 2 verification: District Implementation Committee screening and approval. Step 6: Level 3 verification: National Steering Committee approval and issuance of PM Vishwakarma Certificate & Digital ID Card. Step 7: Undergo 5-7 days basic skill training with ₹500/day stipend. Step 8: Receive ₹15,000 digital toolkit e-voucher/incentive. Step 9: Apply for collateral-free enterprise loan: Tranche 1 up to ₹1 Lakh (at concessional 5% interest), and Tranche 2 up to ₹2 Lakh upon timely repayment.
entries.snippet: End-to-end holistic support for traditional artisans and craftspeople across 18 designated trades, including skill training, ₹15,000 toolkit incentive, and collateral-free credit at 5% interest.

entries.scheme_name: Credit Linked Capital Subsidy Scheme (MSME Champions Scheme)
entries.nodal_ministry: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
entries.text: Credit Linked Capital Subsidy Scheme (MSME Champions Scheme) CLCSS Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises 15% upfront capital subsidy for micro and small enterprises to modernize plant, equipment, and machinery with state-of-the-art technology in 51 approved sub-sectors. Registered Micro and Small Enterprises having valid Udyam Registration. Must be upgrading existing plant and machinery or establishing new facility with proven technology in approved sub-sectors. Loan availed from scheduled commercial banks, state financial corporations, or SIDBI/NABARD. Replacement of obsolete technology with modern energy-efficient machinery. 15% upfront capital subsidy on institutional term loan availed for purchase of eligible machinery, calculated on loan up to ₹1 Crore (Maximum subsidy ₹15 Lakh). machinery technology-upgrade manufacturing capital-subsidy champions Manufacturing Engineering Textiles Food Processing Plastics Chemicals Electronics Online via MSME Champions Single Window Portal Step 1: Enterprise identifies eligible well-established technology / machinery from approved MSME technology list. Step 2: Apply for term loan for technology upgradation through designated Primary Lending Institution (PLI / Bank). Step 3: Lending institution sanctions and disburses loan for machinery acquisition. Step 4: Bank uploads subsidy application claim on MSME Champions / CLCSS online tracking system. Step 5: Nodal agency (SIDBI / NABARD) inspects compliance and forwards claim to Ministry of MSME. Step 6: Ministry approves 15% upfront capital subsidy (capped at ₹15 Lakh on max ₹1 Crore project cost). Step 7: Subsidy funds credited to borrower account and held as term deposit with 3-year lock-in period.
entries.snippet: 15% upfront capital subsidy for micro and small enterprises to modernize plant, equipment, and machinery with state-of-the-art technology in 51 approved sub-sectors.

entries.scheme_name: PM Formalisation of Micro food processing Enterprises Scheme
entries.nodal_ministry: Ministry of Food Processing Industries
entries.text: PM Formalisation of Micro food processing Enterprises Scheme PMFME Ministry of Food Processing Industries Credit-linked financial assistance, technical support, and business upgrade for individual and collective micro food processing units under the One District One Product (ODOP) framework. Existing micro food processing enterprise or new unit aligning with ODOP (One District One Product). Enterprise must have ownership right/long-term lease over premises. Applicant should be above 18 years of age with basic literacy. Beneficiary must contribute at least 10% of the project cost as equity. 35% credit-linked capital subsidy on eligible project cost, with maximum ceiling of ₹10 Lakh per unit. food-processing odop fssai capital-subsidy agro-business Food Processing Agri-Processing Beverages Spices Dairy Bakery Online Portal via MOFPI PMFME Portal Step 1: Visit the official PMFME portal (pmfme.mofpi.gov.in) and register as individual enterprise or group (SHG/FPO/Cooperative). Step 2: Select the designated 'One District One Product' (ODOP) food processing trade or non-ODOP existing processing unit. Step 3: Connect with District Resource Person (DRP) assigned by State Nodal Agency for handholding and DPR preparation. Step 4: Complete online application form detailing proposed machinery, processing capacity, and project cost up to ₹30 Lakh. Step 5: Upload Udyam Certificate, FSSAI registration/license, KYC, bank statements, and Detailed Project Report (DPR). Step 6: District Level Committee (DLC) screens application and recommends it to selected lending bank. Step 7: Bank sanctions credit-linked term loan; 35% capital subsidy (up to ₹10 Lakh) is credited into borrower subsidy reserve fund.
entries.snippet: Credit-linked financial assistance, technical support, and business upgrade for individual and collective micro food processing units under the One District One Product (ODOP) framework.

entries.nodal_ministry: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
entries.text: Agriculture Infrastructure Fund AIF Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare Medium-long term debt financing facility for investment in viable projects for post-harvest management infrastructure and community farming assets. Agri-entrepreneurs, Startups, Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS), FPOs, SHGs, and MSMEs setting up post-harvest management facilities. Eligible projects include cold chains, pack houses, silos, sorting/grading units, assaying units, and ripening chambers. Borrower must have credit approval from participating lending institutions. 3% interest subvention per annum on institutional loans up to ₹2 Crore for a maximum duration of 7 years, along with CGTMSE credit guarantee coverage fee paid by Government. agriculture cold-chain warehousing subvention post-harvest Agriculture Cold Storage Warehousing Food Processing Supply Chain Online Portal via AIF Portal Step 1: Access the Agriculture Infrastructure Fund portal (agriinfra.dac.gov.in) and register as a borrower. Step 2: Choose project category (post-harvest management infrastructure, cold chain, sorting/grading, primary processing, or e-marketing platform). Step 3: Upload Detailed Project Report (DPR), land title / lease documents, Udyam/GSTIN, and promoter background. Step 4: Submit application online; initial scrutiny is conducted by Project Management Unit (PMU) within 7 working days. Step 5: Application routed electronically to borrower's preferred participating lending institution. Step 6: Bank evaluates loan proposal, approves credit facility up to ₹2 Crore with 3% annual interest subvention. Step 7: CGTMSE credit guarantee fee paid by Government of India; loan disbursed in milestone tranches.
entries.snippet: Medium-long term debt financing facility for investment in viable projects for post-harvest management infrastructure and community farming assets.

entries.nodal_ministry: Ministry of Commerce and Industry
entries.text: Startup India Seed Fund Scheme SISFS Ministry of Commerce and Industry Financial assistance to early-stage DPIIT-recognized startups for proof of concept, prototype development, product trials, market entry, and commercialization through approved incubators. Startup recognized by DPIIT, incorporated not more than 2 years ago at the time of application. Startup must have a business idea to develop a product or service with a market fit, viable commercialization, and scope of scaling. Startup should be using technology in its core product or service, or business model. Startup should not have received more than ₹10 Lakh of monetary support under any other Central or State Government scheme (excluding prize money/competitions). Shareholding by Indian promoters in the startup should be at least 51%. Up to ₹20 Lakh grant for Proof of Concept (PoC) / Prototype development / Product trials; Up to ₹50 Lakh through convertible debentures or debt-linked instruments for market entry, commercialization, and scaling. startup seed-fund dpiit prototype convertible-debt innovation ALL Online via Startup India Portal Step 1: Incorporate company as Private Limited or LLP and obtain DPIIT Startup Recognition Certificate on startupindia.gov.in. Step 2: Log in to the official SISFS portal (seedfund.startupindia.gov.in) using Startup India credentials. Step 3: Complete startup profile: innovative business model, proof of concept, commercialization potential, and fund requirement. Step 4: Select up to 3 DPIIT-approved incubators as preferred evaluation partners based on domain/geography. Step 5: Submit pitch deck, prototype demo video/links, and milestone execution roadmap. Step 6: Incubator Seed Management Committee (ISMC) reviews pitch, conducts presentation/interview round. Step 7: Upon selection: Grants up to ₹20 Lakh disbursed in milestone-based tranches for PoC / prototype; Debt/convertible debentures up to ₹50 Lakh disbursed for commercialization.
entries.snippet: Financial assistance to early-stage DPIIT-recognized startups for proof of concept, prototype development, product trials, market entry, and commercialization through approved incubators.

entries.nodal_ministry: Ministry of Commerce and Industry
entries.text: Fund of Funds for Startups FFS Ministry of Commerce and Industry ₹10,000 Crore corpus managed by SIDBI contributing capital to SEBI-registered Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs), which invest directly in innovative DPIIT-recognized startups. Startup must be recognized by DPIIT. Must be incorporated as a Private Limited Company. Company age must not exceed 10 years from the date of incorporation. Startup must demonstrate innovative business model, scalable unit economics, and technology orientation. Venture equity and structured growth capital deployed via SIDBI-partnered Daughter VC Funds (Series Pre-A, Series A, Series B). venture-capital equity sidbi growth-stage dpiit aif ALL Through SEBI-registered Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs) Step 1: Ensure entity is DPIIT-recognized startup with innovative, scalable technology or product proposition. Step 2: Access directory of SIDBI-supported SEBI-registered Daughter Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs) on Startup India portal. Step 3: Prepare comprehensive investor data room: pitch deck, financial model, cap table, and legal due diligence packet. Step 4: Submit pitch proposal directly to partner AIF investment committees matching the startup sector/stage. Step 5: Undergo venture capital evaluation, partner meetings, and formal term sheet negotiation. Step 6: Due diligence completion and execution of Shareholders Agreement (SHA) / Share Subscription Agreement (SSA). Step 7: Equity/quasi-equity capital drawn down from SIDBI FFS commitment directly into startup bank account.
entries.snippet: ₹10,000 Crore corpus managed by SIDBI contributing capital to SEBI-registered Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs), which invest directly in innovative DPIIT-recognized startups.

entries.nodal_ministry: Ministry of Commerce and Industry / Ministry of Finance
entries.text: Section 80-IAC Tax Exemption for Startups 80-IAC Ministry of Commerce and Industry / Ministry of Finance 100% income tax deduction on profits and gains for 3 consecutive financial years out of the first 10 years since incorporation for eligible innovative startups. Incorporated as a Private Limited Company or LLP between April 1, 2016 and March 31, 2025 (or as extended in Finance Act). Total turnover should not exceed ₹100 Crore in any of the previous financial years. Entity must be certified by the Inter-Ministerial Board (IMB) of Certification as an innovative business working towards innovation, development or improvement of products or processes. Company should not be formed by splitting up or reconstruction of an existing business. 100% tax holiday on corporate income profits for any 3 consecutive assessment years chosen by the startup within its first 10 years. tax-holiday 80-iac income-tax dpiit imb-approval innovation ALL Online via Startup India / National Single Window System (NSWS) Step 1: Verify prerequisite: Startup must be Private Limited or LLP incorporated after April 1, 2016, with DPIIT recognition. Step 2: Log in to Startup India Portal and navigate to Section 80-IAC Application Form. Step 3: Upload audited financial statements, ITR returns for preceding financial years, and Memorandum/Articles of Association. Step 4: Provide detailed business deck showcasing innovation, scalable potential for employment generation, and technological differentiation. Step 5: Provide link to product video demonstration / live patent certificates (if filed). Step 6: Submit application to Inter-Ministerial Board (IMB) of Certification. Step 7: IMB evaluates application and issues Section 80-IAC Tax Exemption Certificate, granting 100% tax holiday on profits for 3 consecutive years out of 10.
entries.snippet: 100% income tax deduction on profits and gains for 3 consecutive financial years out of the first 10 years since incorporation for eligible innovative startups.

entries.nodal_ministry: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
entries.text: MeitY SAMRIDH Scheme SAMRIDH Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology Scheme for Accelerating Startups for Scale-up through Mentorship, Funding, and Market Access, matching accelerator investments up to ₹40 Lakh per software tech startup. Software product startup with a demonstrable proof of concept, commercial traction, and customer validations. Must be DPIIT recognized and registered in India. Selected through a partner accelerator empanelled under MeitY SAMRIDH. Indian promoter holding must be greater than 51%. Matched funding up to ₹40 Lakh per startup along with 6-month customized accelerator cohort, corporate pilot linkages, and global investor demo day. software accelerator meity saas msh scaleup Information Technology Software SaaS DeepTech Artificial Intelligence Cybersecurity Online via MeitY Startup Hub (MSH) Portal Step 1: Startup registers on MeitY Startup Hub portal (msh.meity.gov.in). Step 2: Verify eligibility: software product startup with established PoC/early revenue, DPIIT recognition, and Indian-majority shareholding. Step 3: Track and apply to active open cohort calls announced by MeitY SAMRIDH-partnered accelerators. Step 4: Submit comprehensive application detailing software product metrics, traction, customer base, and growth projections. Step 5: Participate in accelerator screening rounds, technical demo evaluation, and pitch day before investment panel. Step 6: Cohort admission: Receive up to ₹40 Lakh matched funding from MeitY alongside equal or higher private co-investment from accelerator/angels. Step 7: Join 6-month customized acceleration program for scaling, enterprise customer pilots, and global market expansion.
entries.snippet: Scheme for Accelerating Startups for Scale-up through Mentorship, Funding, and Market Access, matching accelerator investments up to ₹40 Lakh per software tech startup.

entries.scheme_name: TIDE 2.0 Scheme (Technology Incubation and Development of Entrepreneurs)
entries.nodal_ministry: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
entries.text: TIDE 2.0 Scheme (Technology Incubation and Development of Entrepreneurs) TIDE 2.0 Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology Supports ICT and emerging technology startups (IoT, AI, Blockchain, Robotics) through 51 specialized incubation centers with Entrepreneur-in-Residence (EiR) and prototype grants. Aspiring tech entrepreneurs or early-stage startups working on emerging technology solutions (AI, IoT, Blockchain, CleanTech). Applicant must be incubated or willing to incubate at a recognized TIDE 2.0 incubation center. Focus on solving societal challenges in healthcare, education, agriculture, or financial inclusion. Grant support: Up to ₹7 Lakh for Entrepreneur-in-Residence (EiR) fellows, and up to ₹40 Lakh Grant/Equity for Proof of Concept & commercialization. deeptech iot artificial-intelligence eir incubator-grant Information Technology Artificial Intelligence Robotics IoT Healthcare Tech FinTech Online through designated TIDE 2.0 Incubation Centres Step 1: Ideator / early-stage entrepreneur identifies nearby MeitY TIDE 2.0 Incubation Centre (Tier 1, 2, or 3 academic incubator). Step 2: Select assistance track: Entrepreneur-in-Residence (EiR) for ideation or Grant-in-Aid for prototype development in ICT, IoT, AI, or electronics. Step 3: Submit project proposal detailing ICT innovation, societal impact, and technology development milestones. Step 4: Pitch before Incubator Selection Committee. Step 5: Receive EiR fellowship (up to ₹30,000/month for 12 months) or Grant-in-Aid (up to ₹7 Lakh for prototype development). Step 6: Access maker labs, mentoring, and physical incubation space at host academic institution.
entries.snippet: Supports ICT and emerging technology startups (IoT, AI, Blockchain, Robotics) through 51 specialized incubation centers with Entrepreneur-in-Residence (EiR) and prototype grants.

entries.nodal_ministry: Ministry of Science & Technology - Department of Biotechnology
entries.text: Biotechnology Ignition Grant Scheme BIRAC-BIG Ministry of Science & Technology - Department of Biotechnology Flagship early-stage grant-in-aid of up to ₹50 Lakh for biotech, medtech, diagnostics, agri-biotech, and industrial biotechnology innovations. Biotech startup incorporated for not more than 5 years, or an individual innovator with verified institutional backing. Majority shareholding (> 51%) held by Indian citizens who are researchers, scientists, or medical entrepreneurs. Startups must possess an incubator affiliation or independent laboratory access. Clear scientific hypothesis and novel intellectual property path. Grant-in-aid up to ₹50 Lakh for milestone-based research and proof-of-concept validation over 18 months, with zero equity dilution. biotech medtech diagnostics non-dilutive-grant birac lifesciences Biotechnology Healthcare Medical Devices Agri-Biotech Bio-Pharma Industrial Biotechnology Online via BIRAC Portal during biannual call for proposals Step 1: Register on BIRAC portal (birac.nic.in) during the active call window (typically opens January 1 and July 1). Step 2: Confirm eligibility: Individual biotech innovators or DPIIT-recognized startups incorporated <= 5 years with >= 51% Indian ownership. Step 3: Select a designated BIG Partner (e.g. C-CAMP, IKP Knowledge Park, Venture Center, KIIT-TBI, FITT, BITS Pilani). Step 4: Complete comprehensive technical proposal: unmet medical/industrial need, novelty, preliminary data, and 18-month milestone plan. Step 5: Online technical evaluation by subject matter experts. Step 6: Shortlisted candidates present before Technical Expert Committee (TEC) in-person or online. Step 7: Award of up to ₹50 Lakh as 100% grant-in-aid disbursed in 4-5 milestone-linked tranches.
entries.snippet: Flagship early-stage grant-in-aid of up to ₹50 Lakh for biotech, medtech, diagnostics, agri-biotech, and industrial biotechnology innovations.

entries.scheme_name: Atal Innovation Mission - Seed & Incubation Support
entries.nodal_ministry: NITI Aayog
entries.text: Atal Innovation Mission - Seed & Incubation Support AIM NITI Aayog Catalyzes world-class startups through Atal Incubation Centres (AICs) with prototyping labs, maker spaces, and access to seed grants. Innovators and early-stage ventures working on technology, circular economy, rural development, or high-impact social solutions. Must apply to and be shortlisted by an Atal Incubation Centre (AIC) or Established Incubation Centre (EIC). Clear intent to incorporate a commercial enterprise in India. Incubation access, state-of-the-art laboratory infrastructure, corporate POCs, and micro seed grants ranging from ₹5 Lakh to ₹25 Lakh. niti-aayog incubator prototyping innovation seed-grant ALL Online via AIM NITI Aayog Portal / Atal Incubation Centres Step 1: Innovator or startup identifies designated Atal Incubation Centre (AIC) or Established Incubation Centre (EIC). Step 2: Submit startup application online via AIC incubator cohort application portal. Step 3: Detail problem statement, technological innovation, IP status, and team credentials. Step 4: Undergo evaluation by Incubator Screening Panel and present pitch deck. Step 5: Admission to AIC: Gain physical lab access, fabrication facilities, high-performance computing, and regulatory compliance mentorship. Step 6: Apply for internal seed grants and investor demo day matchmaking facilitated by NITI Aayog.
entries.snippet: Catalyzes world-class startups through Atal Incubation Centres (AICs) with prototyping labs, maker spaces, and access to seed grants.

entries.nodal_ministry: Ministry of Science and Technology - Department of Science & Technology
entries.text: NIDHI-Seed Support System (NIDHI-SSS) NIDHI-SSS Ministry of Science and Technology - Department of Science & Technology Debt and equity seed financing up to ₹1 Crore for technology-driven startups incubated in DST-supported Technology Business Incubators (TBIs). Registered startup incubated in a DST-approved Technology Business Incubator (TBI) for at least 3 months. Focus on commercializing indigenous, science-backed technologies and proprietary engineering. Indian promoter holding must be at least 51%. Financial seed support between ₹25 Lakh and ₹100 Lakh per startup via equity investment, convertible debentures, or soft loan. dst tbi deeptech seed-support equity hardware DeepTech Hardware CleanTech Electronics Materials Science Through DST-supported Technology Business Incubators (TBIs) Step 1: Startup must be an active resident incubatee at a DST-recognized Technology Business Incubator (TBI). Step 2: Formulate seed support application with financial requirements up to ₹1 Crore. Step 3: Submit application to TBI Seed Support Management Committee (SSMC). Step 4: Committee evaluates technological innovation, commercial viability, and repayment/exit capability. Step 5: Approval and execution of investment agreement (equity, convertible debenture, or soft loan). Step 6: Milestone-based fund disbursement into startup escrow account.
entries.snippet: Debt and equity seed financing up to ₹1 Crore for technology-driven startups incubated in DST-supported Technology Business Incubators (TBIs).

entries.scheme_name: PRISM Scheme (Promoting Innovations in Individuals, Start-ups and MSMEs)
entries.nodal_ministry: Ministry of Science and Technology - DSIR
entries.text: PRISM Scheme (Promoting Innovations in Individuals, Start-ups and MSMEs) PRISM Ministry of Science and Technology - DSIR Grants up to ₹50 Lakh for individual innovators and MSMEs to translate novel, green, and industrial technical concepts into marketable working prototypes. Any individual innovator or registered micro/small enterprise with a novel technology idea. Proposal must demonstrate novelty, techno-commercial feasibility, and potential for patent protection. Cost of project evaluated across Phase I (Proof of Concept, max ₹5 Lakh) and Phase II (Working Prototype, max ₹50 Lakh). Grant-in-aid covering up to 90% of project cost for Phase I (up to ₹5 Lakh) and up to 50% of project cost for Phase II (up to ₹50 Lakh). dsir prototype green-technology individual-innovators prism Engineering Green Technology Renewable Energy Waste Management Agriculture Application to nearest PRISM Technology Outreach Co-ordination Centre (TOCIC) Step 1: Download PRISM Application Form (Phase I / Phase II) from DSIR website (dsir.gov.in). Step 2: Prepare detailed proposal on novel invention, working model, and patent search results. Step 3: Submit proposal to nearest designated TOCIC center (hosted at premier IITs, CSIR labs, or university campuses). Step 4: TOCIC undertakes preliminary scrutiny, interviews innovator, and assesses technical feasibility. Step 5: Proposal forwarded to PRISM Project Advisory Committee (PAC) at DSIR headquarters. Step 6: PAC conducts technical presentation round and sanctions grant: Up to ₹2 Lakh for Phase I PoC, ₹20 Lakh for Prototype, or ₹50 Lakh for Enterprise Incubation. Step 7: Grant disbursed in milestone tranches with technical monitoring by assigned TOCIC coordinator.
entries.snippet: Grants up to ₹50 Lakh for individual innovators and MSMEs to translate novel, green, and industrial technical concepts into marketable working prototypes.

entries.nodal_ministry: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
entries.text: GENESIS (Gen-Next Support for Innovative Startups) GENESIS Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology ₹490 Crore umbrella initiative to discover, support, and scale tech startups from Tier-II and Tier-III cities across India with discovery grants and pilot linkages. DPIIT-recognized tech startups registered and operating out of Tier-II and Tier-III cities. Tech-driven product or intellectual property. Indian promoter ownership > 51%. Financial grants up to ₹25 Lakh for pilot rollouts, cloud infrastructure credits, and direct market access partnerships. tier-2-tier-3 meity tech-startups cloud-credits genesis Information Technology Electronic System Design EdTech AgriTech FinTech Online via MeitY Startup Hub Portal Step 1: Register startup profile on MeitY Startup Hub (MSH). Step 2: Verify eligibility: Tech startup operating in Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities across emerging tech domains. Step 3: Apply to open GENESIS calls for acceleration, seed funding, or discovery support. Step 4: Submit pitch presentation focusing on local job creation, digital inclusion, and product roadmaps. Step 5: Participate in virtual screening and regional jury presentation. Step 6: Selection and grant sanction: Access seed funding, cloud infrastructure credits, and corporate partner pilots.
entries.snippet: ₹490 Crore umbrella initiative to discover, support, and scale tech startups from Tier-II and Tier-III cities across India with discovery grants and pilot linkages.

entries.nodal_ministry: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
entries.text: MSME Sustainable (ZED) Certification Scheme MSME-ZED Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Subsidizes comprehensive quality and environmental assessment (Zero Defect, Zero Effect) to enhance competitiveness, reduce waste, and access bank concessions. All manufacturing MSMEs registered with Udyam Registration. Enterprise must undertake the ZED pledge and undergo digital desktop / on-site verification. Valid GST registration required. Financial subsidy on certification cost: 80% for Micro, 60% for Small, 50% for Medium enterprises. Additional 10% subsidy for women/SC/ST owned units. Up to ₹5 Lakh reward for adopting zero-pollution green technology, plus bank loan interest concessions (0.25% - 0.50%). quality zed sustainability qci manufacturing green-certification Manufacturing Online via ZED Portal Step 1: Access official ZED Portal (zed.msme.gov.in) and click 'MSME Registration'. Step 2: Enter valid Udyam Registration Number and mobile number to authenticate. Step 3: Complete online 'ZED Pledge' to commit to Zero Defect Zero Effect principles and obtain instant ZED Pledge Certificate. Step 4: Select desired Certification Level: Bronze, Silver, or Gold. Step 5: Apply for financial subsidy on assessment fees (80% for Micro, 60% for Small, 50% for Medium + 10% for Women/SC/ST). Step 6: Undertake desktop self-assessment or arrange on-site audit by accredited rating agencies (QCI). Step 7: Rectify observed gaps and submit compliance proof. Step 8: Award of official ZED Certificate, unlocking bank interest concessions, free handholding, and testing fee reimbursements.
entries.snippet: Subsidizes comprehensive quality and environmental assessment (Zero Defect, Zero Effect) to enhance competitiveness, reduce waste, and access bank concessions.

entries.nodal_ministry: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
entries.text: MSME Innovative Scheme (Incubation, Design, IPR) MSME-Innovative Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Holistic ecosystem combining Incubation grants, Professional Design subsidies, and IPR reimbursements for patents, trademarks, and design registrations. Any registered MSME with Udyam Registration or student/individual innovator affiliated with an approved Host Institute (HI). Must have an innovative concept, product design challenge, or registered patent/trademark requirement. Commercial potential and technological viability. Financial assistance: Up to ₹15 Lakh for idea incubation; Up to ₹40 Lakh for design project (MSME contribution 25%); Up to ₹5 Lakh reimbursement for Foreign Patent, ₹1 Lakh for Domestic Patent, ₹10,000 for Trademark registration. ipr patent-reimbursement trademark industrial-design incubation champions ALL Online via MSME Innovative Portal Step 1: Log in to MSME Innovative Portal (innovative.msme.gov.in) with Udyam Registration Number. Step 2: Select desired sub-component: Incubation (up to ₹15 Lakh for idea validation), Design (up to ₹40 Lakh for product design), or IPR (up to ₹5 Lakh for patent/trademark/GI filing). Step 3: For Incubation: Select approved Host Institute (HI) / Business Incubator (BI) and upload project concept note. Step 4: Host Institute Project Evaluation Committee (HIPEC) screens idea and uploads recommendation. Step 5: National Project Monitoring and Implementation Unit (PMU) gives final sanction. Step 6: Grant released directly to Host Institute in milestone tranches for equipment, prototyping, and raw material support.
entries.snippet: Holistic ecosystem combining Incubation grants, Professional Design subsidies, and IPR reimbursements for patents, trademarks, and design registrations.

entries.scheme_name: Production Linked Incentive Scheme (PLI) for Large Scale Electronics
entries.nodal_ministry: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
entries.text: Production Linked Incentive Scheme (PLI) for Large Scale Electronics PLI-Electronics Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology Financial incentive of 4% to 6% on incremental sales (over base year) of goods manufactured in India covering mobile phones and specified electronic components. Companies incorporated in India engaged in domestic manufacturing of target electronics products. Must meet minimum threshold criteria of incremental cumulative investment in plant & machinery. Must achieve minimum incremental sales threshold of manufactured goods over the base year. Incentive of 4% to 6% on incremental sales (over base year) of goods manufactured in India for a period of 5 years. pli electronics manufacturing incremental-sales meity Electronics Semiconductor Hardware Manufacturing Online via MeitY ESDM / IFCI PMA Portal Step 1: Monitor notification of application windows by Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY). Step 2: Prepare detailed business expansion plan: target manufacturing category, committed investment, and base year turnover. Step 3: Submit online application on Project Management Agency (PMA - IFCI) portal with requisite non-refundable application fee. Step 4: PMA evaluates eligibility, net worth criteria, and domestic value addition plan. Step 5: Competent Authority / Empowered Committee issues formal approval and baseline acknowledgment letter. Step 6: Execute committed cumulative investment thresholds over specified financial years. Step 7: File annual incentive claims: PMA audits incremental sales of manufactured goods, and disburses 4% to 6% cash incentive on net incremental turnover.
entries.snippet: Financial incentive of 4% to 6% on incremental sales (over base year) of goods manufactured in India covering mobile phones and specified electronic components.

entries.scheme_name: Scheme for Promotion of Manufacturing of Electronic Components and Semiconductors
entries.nodal_ministry: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
entries.text: Scheme for Promotion of Manufacturing of Electronic Components and Semiconductors SPECS Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology Financial incentive of 25% on capital expenditure for the manufacturing of identified electronic components, semiconductor packaging, display fabrication, and active components. Investment in new manufacturing unit or expansion of existing units for eligible electronic items. Minimum capital expenditure investment threshold ranges from ₹5 Crore to ₹1,000 Crore depending on product category. Application must be submitted prior to placing orders for plant and machinery. 25% financial incentive on eligible capital expenditure for plant, machinery, equipment, associated utilities, and clean room facilities. specs semiconductors electronic-components pcb capital-expenditure Electronics Semiconductor Passive Components PCB Hardware Online via MeitY ESDM Portal / IFCI PMA Step 1: Register on MeitY ESDM online portal (meity.gov.in/esdm/specs). Step 2: Identify eligible target goods category (passive components, semiconductors, PCB fabrication, display assembly). Step 3: Prepare Detailed Project Report (DPR) evidencing minimum threshold investment (₹5 Crore to ₹1,000 Crore depending on product). Step 4: Submit application online along with technical equipment lists, quotations, and financial closure plan. Step 5: Technical evaluation by Project Management Agency (IFCI) and approval by Executive Committee. Step 6: Receive formal approval letter specifying commencement window (up to 5 years). Step 7: Purchase, install, and commercialize capital plant & machinery. Step 8: File subsidy claim backed by Chartered Engineer and CA certification: Receive 25% reimbursement on eligible capital expenditure.
entries.snippet: Financial incentive of 25% on capital expenditure for the manufacturing of identified electronic components, semiconductor packaging, display fabrication, and active components.

entries.nodal_ministry: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
entries.text: Procurement and Marketing Support (PMS) Scheme MSME-PMS Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Subsidizes participation in national and international trade fairs, marketing exhibitions, and modern retail packaging to enhance market linkage for MSMEs. Registered manufacturing or service MSMEs holding valid Udyam Registration. Participating in approved trade exhibitions, domestic expos, or onboarding to Government e-Marketplace (GeM). Special priority given to women, SC/ST, and units in North Eastern Region. Up to 100% stall charge reimbursement (up to ₹1.5 Lakh for domestic expos) and reimbursement of packaging and barcode certification costs. trade-fairs marketing exhibitions reimbursement gem-portal ALL Online via MyMSME / MSME Champions Portal Step 1: Register on MyMSME portal (my.msme.gov.in) using Udyam Registration Number. Step 2: Select 'Procurement & Marketing Support Scheme' and choose sub-activity (Trade Fairs, Barcode Adoption, Packaging, E-Commerce onboarding). Step 3: For Trade Fairs: Select recognized domestic or international exhibition from approved calendar and apply at least 1 month prior to event. Step 4: MSME Development and Facilitation Office (DFO) reviews eligibility and recommends stall allotment. Step 5: Participate in trade expo and maintain attendance/stall photographs. Step 6: Submit reimbursement claim form within 45 days along with original stall rent receipt, travel boarding passes, and bank mandate. Step 7: Subsidy credited via Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) into enterprise account (up to 100% stall rent reimbursement for Women/SC/ST Micro units).
entries.snippet: Subsidizes participation in national and international trade fairs, marketing exhibitions, and modern retail packaging to enhance market linkage for MSMEs.

entries.nodal_ministry: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
entries.text: National SC-ST Hub (NSSH) Scheme NSSH Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Specialized affirmative support ecosystem to empower SC/ST micro and small entrepreneurs to fulfill the 4% mandatory public procurement quota by CPSEs and ministries. Enterprise owned by SC/ST entrepreneurs (100% ownership in sole proprietorship, or at least 51% equity in partnership/company). Valid Udyam Registration and Caste Certificate of promoter. Applicant must be engaged in manufacturing or provision of services. 100% reimbursement of Single Point Registration Scheme (SPRS) fees, 100% annual credit guarantee fee reimbursement under CGTMSE, up to ₹1 Lakh subsidy for trade fairs, and subsidized tender document fees. sc-st affirmative-action nsic cgtmse-fee-reimbursement public-procurement ALL Online via National SC-ST Hub Portal or nearest NSIC Branch Step 1: Enterprise must have valid Udyam Registration with >= 51% shareholding by SC/ST entrepreneurs. Step 2: Register on National SC-ST Hub portal (scsthub.in) or visit local NSIC office. Step 3: Upload Caste Certificate, Udyam Certificate, PAN, and Bank details. Step 4: Apply for desired interventions: Single Point Registration Scheme (SPRS) fee waiver, Special Marketing Assistance, or vendor development registration. Step 5: Connect with Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs) to participate in mandatory 4% public procurement reserved for SC/ST enterprises. Step 6: Submit fee reimbursement claims for quality certifications (ISO/BIS/ZED) and barcode registration. Step 7: Direct subsidy reimbursement credited into applicant bank account.
entries.snippet: Specialized affirmative support ecosystem to empower SC/ST micro and small entrepreneurs to fulfill the 4% mandatory public procurement quota by CPSEs and ministries.

entries.nodal_ministry: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
entries.text: International Cooperation (IC) Scheme MSME-IC Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Financial assistance to MSMEs for participating in international exhibitions, trade fairs, buyer-seller meets, and technology transfer delegations abroad. Registered MSME with valid Udyam Registration and active IEC (Import Export Code). Must have an operational track record of at least 1 year. Participating in international fairs or business delegations approved under the IC guidelines. Reimbursement of 100% economy class airfare (up to ₹1.5 Lakh) and 100% space/stall rent (up to ₹3 Lakh) for individual MSME exporters participating in foreign events. export international-trade airfare-reimbursement global-fairs iec ALL Online via IC Scheme Portal Step 1: Industry association or MSME enterprise logs in to the official IC Scheme Portal (ic.msme.gov.in). Step 2: Select relevant sub-component: Market Development Assistance (MDA) for international trade delegations, participating in international exhibitions, or organizing international conferences. Step 3: Submit application online at least 60 days before the scheduled international event. Step 4: Upload event brochure, organizer confirmation, participant list with Udyam numbers, and proposed budget. Step 5: Screening Committee in Ministry of MSME reviews proposal and issues in-principle sanction. Step 6: Participate in international exhibition/delegation abroad. Step 7: Submit post-event claim within 90 days with airfare receipts, stall invoice, visa stamps, and event outcome report to receive financial reimbursement.
entries.snippet: Financial assistance to MSMEs for participating in international exhibitions, trade fairs, buyer-seller meets, and technology transfer delegations abroad.

entries.nodal_ministry: Ministry of Textiles
entries.text: Amended Technology Upgradation Fund Scheme (ATUFS) ATUFS Ministry of Textiles Capital investment subsidy for the modernization and technology induction in textile segments including garmenting, technical textiles, weaving, and processing. Entity engaged in textile manufacturing intending to install benchmarked state-of-the-art machinery. Must obtain Unique Identification Number (UID) from i-TUFS portal prior to machinery acquisition. Term loan availed from notified lending banks/financial institutions. Capital Investment Subsidy (CIS) of 10% to 15% on eligible benchmarked machinery with a subsidy ceiling up to ₹30 Crore depending on textile sub-segment. textiles garmenting capital-investment-subsidy atufs machinery-modernization Textiles & Apparel Technical Textiles Garmenting Weaving Spinning Online via i-TUFS Portal (Office of the Textile Commissioner) Step 1: Textile manufacturing entity registers on i-TUFS portal (itufs.gov.in) with Udyam and PAN. Step 2: Apply for term loan through an empaneled lending agency (Scheduled Commercial Bank). Step 3: Lending agency sanctions loan and uploads term loan details on i-TUFS portal. Step 4: System generates Unique Identification Number (UID) for each machine to be procured. Step 5: Procure eligible benchmarked machinery from approved machinery manufacturers. Step 6: Physical joint inspection conducted by Office of Textile Commissioner and lending bank. Step 7: Capital Investment Subsidy (10% to 15% capped at ₹20-30 Crore depending on garmenting/technical textile sector) released directly into borrower loan escrow account.
entries.snippet: Capital investment subsidy for the modernization and technology induction in textile segments including garmenting, technical textiles, weaving, and processing.

entries.scheme_name: ASPIRE (Scheme for Promotion of Innovation, Rural Industry & Entrepreneurship)
entries.nodal_ministry: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
entries.text: ASPIRE (Scheme for Promotion of Innovation, Rural Industry & Entrepreneurship) ASPIRE Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Sets up Livelihood Business Incubators (LBIs) and Technology Business Incubators (TBIs) to promote rural agro-business enterprise creation and employment. Agro-rural entrepreneurs, educational institutions, or technical bodies setting up LBI/TBI incubators in rural/semi-urban areas. Focus on skilling youth and translating rural produce into value-added enterprise goods. One-time 100% grant of up to ₹1 Crore for government agencies and up to ₹50 Lakh for private bodies for plant and machinery procurement for LBI incubators. rural-industry lbi tbi agro-business aspire incubation Agro-Rural Industry Food Processing Rural Entrepreneurship Handicrafts Online via ASPIRE MSME Portal Step 1: Eligible implementing agency (government institute, university, R&D lab, or industry association) visits ASPIRE portal (aspire.msme.gov.in). Step 2: Select component: Setting up Livelihood Business Incubator (LBI) or Technology Business Incubator (TBI) in agro-rural sector. Step 3: Prepare Detailed Project Report (DPR) detailing local agro-rural raw materials, proposed training machinery, and skill incubation plans. Step 4: Submit application online to Ministry of MSME. Step 5: Project Screening Committee (PSC) evaluates DPR and technical viability. Step 6: Approval by Scheme Steering Committee (SSC): 100% grant of up to ₹1 Crore for government LBIs (or ₹75 Lakh for private LBIs) for plant and machinery procurement. Step 7: Fund disbursement in tranches for procurement, commissioning, and continuous training of rural entrepreneurs.
entries.snippet: Sets up Livelihood Business Incubators (LBIs) and Technology Business Incubators (TBIs) to promote rural agro-business enterprise creation and employment.

entries.nodal_ministry: Industries Department, Government of Maharashtra
entries.text: Chief Minister Employment Generation Programme (Maharashtra) CMEGP-MH Industries Department, Government of Maharashtra State flagship credit-linked subsidy scheme for youth and micro-entrepreneurs setting up manufacturing and service ventures in Maharashtra. Domicile resident of Maharashtra state aged 18 to 45 years (up to 50 years for SC/ST/Women/Ex-servicemen). Minimum 7th standard pass for project cost up to ₹10 Lakh, and 10th standard pass for project cost above ₹10 Lakh. Project must be located within the state of Maharashtra. Only for new micro-enterprises in manufacturing (up to ₹50 Lakh) or service (up to ₹20 Lakh). 15% to 35% capital subsidy (margin money) on project cost up to ₹50 Lakh for manufacturing and ₹20 Lakh for service units. maharashtra state-scheme cmegp margin-money dic youth-employment ALL Online via Maha-CMEGP Portal Step 1: Visit official Maharashtra CMEGP portal (maha-cmegp.gov.in) and click 'Applicant Registration'. Step 2: Enter Aadhaar number, name, domicile of Maharashtra, and date of birth (18-45 years, or up to 50 for SC/ST/Women). Step 3: Fill project details: Manufacturing (cost up to ₹50 Lakh) or Service/Agro-processing (cost up to ₹20 Lakh). Step 4: Upload educational certificate (minimum Class 7th or 10th depending on cost), domicile certificate, caste certificate (if applicable), and Project Report. Step 5: Select Sponsoring Agency: District Industries Centre (DIC) or Maharashtra State Khadi and Village Industries Board (KVIB). Step 6: Select preferred financing bank branch within Maharashtra. Step 7: District Level Task Force Committee (DLTFC) chaired by District Collector screens application and conducts interview. Step 8: Recommended application forwarded to bank; bank sanctions composite credit. Step 9: Complete 2-week mandatory EDP training; Government of Maharashtra disburses 15% to 35% margin money subsidy directly into bank account with 3-year lock-in.
entries.snippet: State flagship credit-linked subsidy scheme for youth and micro-entrepreneurs setting up manufacturing and service ventures in Maharashtra.
